- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 1–3% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops >2% from recent peak, model underestimates further decline; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% for next 7–14 days.
- Model consistently overpredicts mean reversion in 30-day horizon; for 30d forecasts, apply 0.5–1.5% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows 3+ consecutive 0.00 values, model tends to ignore volatility; add 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to forecast if price is trending down.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows >3 consecutive days below 65.00, model often fails to recognize sustained decline; apply 1–2% downward bias for next 10 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise; use 0.5–1.0% smoothing filter on 30d forecast to reduce overfitting.
